articleTitle: Omega results for the divisor and circle problems
abstract: We obtain new omega results for the error terms in two classical lattice point problems. These results are likely to be the best possible.

articleTitle: Birational unboundedness of ℚ-Fano threefolds
abstract: We prove that the family of ℚ-Fano threefolds with Picard number one is birationally unbounded.

articleTitle: Moments and cumulants of polynomial random variables on unitarygroups, the Itzykson-Zuber integral, and free probability
abstract: We consider integrals on unitary groups U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\int_{{\text{?U}}_d}U_{i_1\text{?}j_1}\cdots U_{i_q\text{?}j_q}U_{{j^{'}}_1{i^{'}}_1}^\ast\cdots U_{{j^{'}}_{q^{'}}{i^{'}}_{q^{'}}}^{\ast} dU$</tex> . We give an explicit formula in terms of characters of symmetric groups and Schur functions, which allows to rederive an asymptotic expansion as d → ∞. Using this, we rederive and strengthen a result of asymptotic freeness due to Voiculescu. We then study large d asymptotics of matrix-model integrals and of the logarithm of Itzykson-Zuber integrals and show that they converge towards a limit when considered as power series. In particular, we give an explicit formula for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\text{lim}}_{d\rightarrow\infty}{(\partial^n/\partial z^n\text{?})}d^{-2}\text{?log}\int_{{\text{U}}_d}e^{zd\text{?Tr}{(XUYU^\ast)}}dU\vert_{z=0}$</tex> , assuming that the normalized traces d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>Tr(X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>) and d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>Tr (Y<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>) converge in the large d limit. We consider as well a different scaling and relate its asymptotics to Voiculescu's R-transform.

articleTitle: Uniform asymptotics for polynomials orthogonal with respect to a general class of discrete weights and universality results for associated ensembles: announcement of results
abstract: We compute the pointwise asymptotics of polynomials orthogonal with respect to a general class of pure point measures supported on finite sets as both the number of nodes of the measure and also the degree of the orthogonal polynomials become large. The class of orthogonal polynomials we consider includes as special cases the Krawtchouk and Hahn classical discrete orthogonal polynomials, but is far more general. In particular, we consider nodes that are not necessarily equally spaced. The asymptotic results are given with error bound for all points in the complex plane except for a finite union of discs of arbitrarily small but fixed radii. These exceptional discs are the neighborhoods of the so-called band edges of the associated equilibrium measure. As applications, we prove universality results for correlation functions of a general class of discrete orthogonal polynomial ensembles, and in particular we deduce asymptotic formulae with error bound for certain statistics relevant in the random tiling of a hexagon with rhombus-shaped tiles. The discrete orthogonal polynomials are characterized in terms of a Riemann-Hilbert problem formulated for a meromorphic matrix with certain pole conditions. By extending the methods of Kamvissis, McLaughlin, and Miller, we suggest a general and unifying approach to handle Riemann-Hilbert problems in the situation when poles of the unknown matrix are accumulating on some set in the asymptotic limit of interest.

articleTitle: L2 stability of solitons for KdV equation
abstract: We prove stability and asymptotic stability in L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of solitons for Korteweg-de Vries equation on the whole line from the use of the Miura transformation. Asymptotic stability of kinks for modified KdV equation is also considered.

articleTitle: On Mackey's irreducibility criterion for induced representations
abstract: Let G be a discrete group, H a subgroup of G, and σ a unitary representation of H. We give an example showing that Mackey's irreducibility criterion for the induced representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ind}_H^G\text{?}\sigma$</tex> does not apply when σ is infinite dimensional.

articleTitle: Frobenius splitting and ordinarity
abstract: We examine the relationship between the notion of Frobenius splitting and ordinarity for varieties. We show that the de Rham-Witt cohomology groups H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sup>(X,W(O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf>)) of a smooth projective Frobenius split variety are finitely generated over W(k). We provide counterexamples to a conjecture of Mehta that Frobenius split varieties are ordinary or even Hodge-Witt.

articleTitle: A ring version of Mazur's conjecture on topology of rational points
abstract: Barry Mazur has conjectured that the topological closure of any variety V(ℚ) in V(ℝ) possesses at most a finite number of connected components. We consider this conjecture in a ring setting. Given an integrally closed subring R of a number field, we investigate the number of connected components of the topological closure of V(R) in ℝ or ℂ.

articleTitle: Maass cusp forms with quadratic integer coefficients
abstract: We prove that any Maass cusp form whose normalized L-series coefficients lie in a quadratic extension of Q, with one field excepted, must be of Galois type. The proof, which makes integral use of the symmetric second, third, and fourth power automorphic lifts on GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, is accomplished under a condition on the Galois action on the form.

articleTitle: Problème de Mordell-Lang modulo certaines sous-variétés abéliennes
abstract: Following a result of Bombieri, Masser, and Zannier on tori, the second author proved that the intersection of a transversal curve C in a power E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sup> of a C. M. elliptic curve with the union of all algebraic subgroups of E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sup> of codimension 2 is finite. Here transversal means that C is not contained in any translate of an algebraic subgroup of codimension 1. We merge this result with Faltings' theorem that C∩Γ is finite when Γ is a finite rank subgroup of E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sup>. We obtain the finiteness of the intersection of C with the union of all Γ+B for Ban abelian subvariety of codimension 2. As a corollary, we generalize the previous result to a curve C not contained in any proper algebraic subgroup, but possibly contained in a translate. We also have weaker analog results in the non C. M. case.

articleTitle: Equilibrium distribution of zeros of random polynomials
abstract: We consider ensembles of random polynomials of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p{(z)}=\sum\nolimits_{j=1}^{\text{?}N}a_j\text{??}P_j$</tex> , where the a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf> are independent complex normal random variables and where the P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf> are the orthonormal polynomials on the boundary of a bounded simply connected analytic plane domain Ω⊂ℂ relative to an analytic weight ρ(z)|dz|. In the simplest case where Ω is the unit disk and ρ = 1, so that P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf>(z) = z<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</sup>, it is known that the average distribution of zeros is the uniform measure on S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>. We show that for any analytic (Ω,ρ), the zeros of random polynomials almost surely become equidistributed relative to the equilibrium measure on ∂Ω as N → ∞. We further show that on the length scale of 1/N, the correlations have a universal scaling limit independent of (Ω,ρ).

articleTitle: Extension of unitary Virasoro vertex operator algebra by a simple module
abstract: We study a certain extension of the Virasoro vertex operator algebra L(c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>,0), where the central charge c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> = 1 − 6/(m + 2)(m + 3), and m = 1,2,…. We show that the space L(c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>,0)⊕ L(c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>,h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>) has a vertex operator algebra (or superalgebra) structure for some h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>. When L(c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>,0)⊕ L(c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>,h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup> is a vertex operator algebra (VOA), we classify all of its irreducible modules and show that L(c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>,0)⊕ L(c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>,h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup> is rational. In addition, the fusion rules among irreducible L(c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>,0)⊕ L(c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>,h<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>-modules are completely determined.

articleTitle: On the nonnegativity of Rankin-Selberg L-functions at the center of symmetry
abstract: Let π and π′ be self-dual cuspidal representations of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(A) and GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n′</inf>(A), respectively. Assume that π and π′ have opposite self-duality types. We prove that L(1/2,π⊗π′)≥ 0.

articleTitle: Zeros of polynomials orthogonal on several intervals
Periods of Hilbert modular forms and rational points on elliptic curves
abstract: Let E be a modular elliptic curve over a totally real field. A conjecture of the first author allows the construction of canonical algebraic points on E by suitably integrating the associated Hilbert modular form. The main goal of the present paper is to obtain numerical evidence for this conjecture in the first case where it asserts something nontrivial, namely, when E has everywhere good reduction over a real quadratic field.

articleTitle: Toric Fano varieties and birational morphisms
abstract: We study smooth toric Fano varieties using primitive relations and toric Mori theory. We show that for any irreducible invariant divisor D in a toric Fano variety X, we have 0≤ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf>-ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>≤ 3 for the difference of the Picard numbers of X and D. Moreover, if ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf>-ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>>0 (with some additional hypotheses if ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf>-ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>=1), we give an explicit birational description of X. Using this result, we show that when dim X=5, we have ρ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf>≤ 9. Then, we study equivariant morphisms whose source is Fano. We give some general results, and in dimension 4, we show that a birational equivariant morphism is always a composite of smooth equivariant blowups. Finally, we study under which hypotheses a nonprojective toric variety can become Fano after a smooth equivariant blowup.

articleTitle: The area of a minimal embedded 2-sphere in a manifold diffeomorphic to S3
abstract: It is known that each Riemannian manifold Σ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> diffeomorphic to S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> contains an embedded minimal submanifold diffeomorphic to S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The goal of this paper is to give an upper bound for the minimal area of an embedded minimal S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in terms of the diameter, volume, and curvature of Σ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Welschinger invariant and enumeration of real rational curves
abstract: Welschinger's invariant bounds from below the number of real rational curves through a given generic collection of real points in the real projective plane. We estimate this invariant using Mikhalkin's approach which deals with a corresponding count of tropical curves. In particular, our estimate implies that, for any positive integer d, there exists a real rational curve of degree d through any collection of 3d−1 real points in the projective plane, and, moreover, asymptotically in the logarithmic scale at least one third of the complex plane rational curves through a generic point collection are real. We also obtain similar results for curves on other toric Del Pezzo surfaces.

articleTitle: Global carleman estimates for weak solutions of elliptic nonhomogeneous Dirichlet problems
abstract: We consider weak solutions of a general second-order elliptic equation with right-hand side <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f+\sum\nolimits_{j=0}^N\partial f_j/\partial x_j\in H^{-1}{(\Omega)}$</tex> with f, f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf> ∈ L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(Ω) and boundary trace g ∈ H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>(Γ). We prove a global Carleman estimate for the solution y of this equation in terms of the weighted L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-norms of f and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf> and the H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>-norm of g. This estimate depends on two real parameters s and λ which are supposed to be large enough, and is sharp with respect to the exponents of these parameters. This allows us to obtain, for example, sharper estimates on the pressure term in linearized Navier-Stokes equations and it turns out to be very useful in the context of controllability problems.

articleTitle: Lower bounds for the number of closed billiard trajectories of period 2 and 3 in manifolds embedded in Euclidean space
abstract: Let T ⊂ ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> be a smooth strictly convex domain bounded by a smooth curve M = ∂ T. The billiard ball is a point which moves in T along a straight line and rebounds from M making the angle of incidence equal to the angle of reflection. The classical problem by G. Birkhoff is to find the lower estimate for the number of closed billiard trajectories with p reflection points. In this paper, we give a definition of a periodic billiard trajectory in a smooth closed m-dimensional manifold M ⊂ ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, find a lower bound for the number of 3-periodic billiard trajectories, and give a new proof of P. Pushkar's estimate for 2-periodic trajectories.

articleTitle: Representations of semisimple lattices in mapping class groups
abstract: We show that any homomorphism from a lattice of a quaternionic or Cayley hyperbolic space to a mapping class group has finite image. Together with earlier results of Ivanov (1992), Kaimanovich and Masur (1996), and Farb and Masur (1998) on the higher-rank cases, this gives a complete picture about superrigidity of representations of semisimple lattices in mapping class groups.

articleTitle: On the Poincare series of quadratic algebras associated to Hecke symmetries
abstract: Hecke symmetries generalize the usual tensor symmetry of vector spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v\otimes w\mapsto w\otimes v$</tex> as well as the symmetry of vector superspaces. To a Hecke symmetry there associates a quadratic algebra which can be interpreted as the function algebra upon a certain quantum space. This paper investigates the Poincaré series of this quadratic algebra. We show that it is a rational function with numerator and denominator being a reciprocal polynomial and a skew-reciprocal polynomial, respectively.

articleTitle: Uniqueness of braidings of quasitriangular Lie bialgebras and lifts of classical r-Matrices
abstract: It is known that any quantization of a quasitriangular Lie bialgebra g gives rise to a braiding on the dual Poisson-Lie formal group G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>. We show that this braiding always coincides with the Weinstein-Xu braiding. We show that this braiding is the “time one automorphism” of a Hamiltonian vector field, corresponding to a certain formal function on G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> × G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>, the “lift of r,” which can be expressed in terms of r by universal formulas. The lift of r coincides with the classical limit of the rescaled logarithm of any R-matrix quantizing it.

articleTitle: Eigenvalues and holonomy
abstract: We estimate the eigenvalues of connection Laplacians in terms of the nontriviality of the holonomy. Our basic analytic and geometric tools are a Sobolev inequality of Gallot, a suitable Bochner formula, and Moser iteration.

articleTitle: Theta functions and Szegö kernels
abstract: We study relations between two fundamental constructions associated to vector bundles on a smooth complex projective curve; the theta function (a section of a line bundle on the moduli space of vector bundles) and the Szegö kernel (a section of a vector bundle on the square of the curve). Two types of relations are demonstrated. First, we establish a higher-rank version of the prime form, describing the pullback of determinant line bundles by difference maps, and show that the theta function pulls back to the determinant of the Szegö kernel. Next, we prove that the expansion of the Szegö kernel at the diagonal gives the logarithmic derivative of the theta function over the moduli space of bundles for a fixed, or moving, curve. In particular, we recover the identification of the space of connections on the theta line bundle with moduli space of flat vector bundles, when the curve is fixed. When the curve varies, we identify this space of connections with the moduli space of extended connections, which we introduce.

articleTitle: Characterization of the spectrum of Schrödinger operators with periodic distributions
abstract: Consider the Schrödinger operator L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf> = −y″+q′y on L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(ℝ) with a distribution q′, where q ∈ L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(0,1) is a 1-periodic function. The spectrum of L is purely absolutely continuous and consists of intervals separated by gaps. We solve the inverse problem (including characterization) both in terms of vertical slits on the quasimomentum domain and in terms of gap lengths. Furthermore, we obtain a priori two-sided estimates for these maps. In addition, we solve the inverse problem and obtain the two-sided estimates for the Riccati map. Using these results we determine various asymptotics for our operator: asymptotics of the gap lengths, of periodic spectrum, and of the Dirichlet eigenvalues.

articleTitle: Approximation and convergence of formal CR-mappings
abstract: Let M⊂ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup> be a minimal real-analytic CR-submanifold and M′⊂ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N′</sup> a real-algebraic subset through points p ∈ M and p′ ∈ M′, N,N′≥ 2. We show that any formal (holomorphic) mapping f : (ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup>,p) → (ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N′</sup>,p′), sending M into M′, can be approximated up to any given order at p by a convergent map sending M into M′. If M is furthermore generic, we also show that any such map f that is not convergent must send (in an appropriate sense) M into the set E′⊂ M′ of points of D'Angelo infinite type. Therefore, if M′ does not contain any nontrivial complex-analytic subvariety through p′, any formal map f as above is necessarily convergent.

articleTitle: Coboundary dynamical Poisson groupoids and integrable systems
abstract: We present a general scheme to construct integrable systems based on realization in the coboundary dynamical Poisson groupoids of Etingof and Varchenko. We also present a factorization method for solving the Hamiltonian flows. To illustrate our scheme and factorization theory, we consider a family of hyperbolic spin Ruijsenaars-Schneider models related to affine Toda field theories and solve the equations of motion in a simple case.

articleTitle: Small representations for odd orthogonal groups
abstract: If 2n + 1 ≥ 9, Vogan (1981) has shown that there is no representation of SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+1</inf> or a metaplectic cover attached to the minimal coadjoint orbit. Thus, there are no small representations in the standard sense. In this paper, representations of the metaplectic double cover of SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+1</inf> are constructed both locally and globally, and it is shown that these representations are small in the sense that they are attached to one of the next smallest coadjoint orbits with respect to the standard partial ordering. The global automorphic representations are shown to be square integrable and the vanishing properties of their Fourier coefficients are established.

articleTitle: On the rigidity for conformally compact Einstein manifolds
abstract: We prove that a conformally compact Einstein manifold with the round sphere as its conformal infinity has to be the hyperbolic space. We do not assume the manifolds to be spin, but our approach relies on the positive mass theorem for asymptotic flat manifolds. The proof is based on the understanding of positive eigenfunctions and compactifications obtained by positive eigenfunctions.

articleTitle: Lower bounds for the canonical height on elliptic curves over abelian extensions
abstract: Let K be a number field and let E/K be an elliptic curve. If E has complex multiplication, we show that there is a positive lower bound for the canonical height of nontorsion points on E defined over the maximal abelian extension K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ab</sup> of K. This is analogous to results of Amoroso, Dvornicich (2000) and Amoroso, Zannier (2000) for the multiplicative group. We also show that if E has nonintegral j-invariant (so that, in particular, E does not have complex multiplication), then there exists C > 0 such that there are only finitely many points P ∈ E(K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ab</sup>) of canonical height less than C. This strengthens a result of Hindry and Silverman (1990).

articleTitle: Regularity of solutions of the heat equation on a cone
abstract: We study the differentiability properties of solutions to the heat equation on a cone manifold. The heat operator considered here is that which corresponds to the Friedrichs extension of the Laplacian. For initial data in appropriately defined Hölder spaces, the estimates are good enough to prove short-time existence of solutions of certain semilinear parabolic equations.

articleTitle: Existence of minimizing Willmore surfaces of prescribed genus
abstract: Let rβ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> ≥ 4π be the infimum of the Willmore functional, that is, the integral of the squared mean curvature, among orientable, closed, genus p surfaces immersed in ℝ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>. In the case p ≥ 2, Simon (1993) proved that rβ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> is attained, if the strict inequality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm{r\beta}}_p<{\mathrm{r\beta}}_{p_{\text{?}1}}+{\mathrm{r\beta}}_{p_{\text{?}2}}-4\text{?}\pi$</tex> is satisfied whenever p = p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> + p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> for p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> ≥ 1. We prove this condition, and hence the existence of minimizers for p ≥ 2, by explicitly constructing a comparison surface which is a connected sum of the minimizers for genus p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: Finite-dimensional representations of rational Cherednik algebras
abstract: A complete classification and character formulas for finite-dimensional irreducible representations of the rational Cherednik algebra of type A are given. Less complete results for other types are obtained. Links to the geometry of affine flag manifolds and Hilbert schemes are discussed.

articleTitle: Spectral triples from Mumford curves
abstract: We construct spectral triples associated to Schottky-Mumford curves, in such a way that the local Euler factor can be recovered from the zeta functions of such spectral triples. We propose a way of extending this construction to the case where the curve is not k-split degenerate.

articleTitle: 3-state potts model, Moonshine vertex operator algebra,and 3A-elements of the monster group
abstract:
We show that the Moonshine vertex operator algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V^
atural$</tex> contains a subalgebra T isomorphic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(M^	au\otimes(L	ext{?}(4/5,0)\oplus	ext{?}L	ext{?}(4/5,3)))^{12}$</tex> , where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M=L	ext{?}{(1/2,0)}\otimes	ext{?}L	ext{?}{(7/10,0)}\oplus	ext{?}L	ext{?}{(1/2,1/2)}\otimes	ext{?}L	ext{?}{(7/10,3/2)}$</tex> and τ is an automorphism of order 3 of M using a ℤ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-orbifold construction of the Moonshine vertex operator algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V^

Moreover, the explicit actions of certain 3A-elements of the Monster simple group on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V^
