articleTitle: A construction of CAP representations in classical groups
abstract: We introduce a new construction for CAP representations for classical groups. Let τ be a cuspidal representation on GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2m</inf>(A) such that the exterior square L-function has a pole at s=1. Given a cuspidal representation σ on SP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n</inf>(A), we associate with the pair τ and σ a representation on SP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+4m</inf>(A) which is associated with the parabolic subgroup whose Levi part is GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2m</inf>×SP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n</inf>. We show that under certain conditions the representation obtained is a CAP representation on SP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+4m</inf>(A). The method we use is by introducing a kernel function on a big group, then using some unipotent integration we restrict to a certain dual pair which produces the lifting.

articleTitle: A poisson summation formula and lower bounds for resonances in hyperbolic manifolds
abstract: For convex cocompact hyperbolic manifolds of dimension n+1, we derive a Poisson-type formula for scattering resonances which may be regarded as a version of Selberg's trace formula for these manifolds. Using techniques of Guillopé and Zworski, we easily obtain an OR<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n+1</sup>) lower bound for the counting function for scattering resonances together with other lower bounds for the counting function of resonances in strips.

articleTitle: Twisted modules for vertex operator algebras and Bernoulli polynomials
abstract: Using general principles of the theory of vertex operator algebras and their twisted modules, we obtain a bosonic, twisted construction of a certain central extension of a Lie algebra of differential operators on the circle, for an arbitrary twisting automorphism. The construction involves the Bernoulli polynomials in a fundamental way. This is explained through results in the general theory of vertex operator algebras, including a new identity, which we call “modified weak associativity.” This paper is an announcement. The detailed proofs will appear elsewhere.

articleTitle: Exceptional parameters for generic A-hypergeometric systems
abstract: The holonomic rank of an A-hypergeometric system H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf>rβ is conjectured to be independent of the parameter vector rβ if and only if the toric ideal I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf> is Cohen-Macaulay. We prove this conjecture in the case that I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf> is generic by explicitly constructing more than the expected number of linearly independent hypergeometric functions for parameters rβ coming from embedded primes of certain initial ideals of I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf>. We also show, under no assumptions on A, that its exceptional set E(A) is Zariski constructible.

articleTitle: The Asai transfer to GL4 via the Langlands-Shahidi method
abstract: We establish a particular instance of Langlands functoriality. Namely, if E/F is a quadratic extension of number fields, we produce the automorphic transfer from GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</inf>) to GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>(A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>) corresponding to the Asai representation. We prove this by applying the converse theorem of Cogdell and Piatetski-Shapiro to analytic properties of certain L-functions obtained from the Langlands-Shahidi method. We conclude the paperby determining the fibers of the Asai transfer.

articleTitle: On the projections of measures invariant under the geodesic flow
abstract: We consider general probability measures μ on SM, the unit tangent bundle of a Riemannian surface M, invariant under the geodesic flow, and study their projection to M. We show that if dim μ ≤ dim M(= 2) the projected measure has the same dimension as μ, and if dim μ > dim M the projection is regular with respect to the Lebesgue measure on M.

articleTitle: Finite rank vector bundles on inductive limits of grassmannians
abstract: If ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup> is the projective ind-space, that is, ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup> is the inductive limit of linear embeddings of complex projective spaces, the Barth-Van de Ven-Tyurin (BVT) theorem claims that every finite rank vector bundle on ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup> is isomorphic to a direct sum of line bundles. We extend this theorem to general sequences of morphisms between projective spaces by proving that, if there are infinitely many morphisms of degree higher than one, every vector bundle of finite rank on the inductive limit is trivial. We then establish a relative version of these results, and apply it to the study of vector bundles on inductive limits of grassmannians. In particular we show that the BVT Theorem extends to the ind-Grassmannian of subspaces commensurable with a fixed infinite-dimensional and infinite-codimensional subspace in ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup>. We also show that, for a class of twisted ind-Grassmannians, every finite rank vector bundle is trivial.

articleTitle: Connected components of the space of surface group representations
abstract: Let G be a connected, compact, semisimple Lie group. It is known that for a compact closed orientable surface Σ of genus ℓ > 1, the order of the group H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(Σ,π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(G)) is equal to the number of connected components of the space Hom(π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(Σ),G)/G which can also be identified with the moduli space of gauge equivalence classes of flat G-bundles over Σ. We show that the same statement for a closed compact nonorientable surface which is homeomorphic to the connected sum of m copies of the real projective plane, where m ≠ 1,2,4, can be easily derived from a result in A. Alekseev, A. Malkin, and E. Meinrenken's recent work on Lie group-valued moment maps (1998).

articleTitle: On the boundary of the Milnor fibre of nonisolated singularities
abstract: We announce several results on the topology of the holomorphic germs f : (ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>,0) → (ℂ,0) which have a 1-dimensional critical locus: the boundary of the Milnor fibre of f admits a Waldhausen structure, and the vertical monodromies along the critical locus are periodic. This leads to a topological characterization of the reduced germs which have an isolated singularity. Namely, a reduced germ f : (ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>,0) → (ℂ,0) has an isolated singularity at 0 if and only if the boundary of its Milnor fibre is homeomorphic to the link of the normalization of f<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>(0). On the boundary of the Milnor fibre of nonisolated singularities (erratum) dx.doi.org/10.1155/S1073792804139998

articleTitle: On the Hodge-Newton decomposition for split groups
abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to prove a group-theoretic generalization of a theorem of Katz on isocrystals. Along the way, we reprove the group-theoretic generalization of Mazur's inequality for isocrystals due to Rapoport and Richartz, and generalize, from split groups to unramified groups, a result of Kottwitz and Rapoport which determines when the affine Deligne-Lusztig subset <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X_\mu^G{(b)}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G{(L)}/G{({\text{o}}_L)}$</tex> is nonempty.

articleTitle: Difference analogs of elliptic KdV solitons and Schrödingeroperators
abstract: We study elliptic solutions to difference analogs of soliton equations and their connections with finite-gap Schrödinger difference operators. We generalize the algebro geometric approach of elliptic (KDV) solitons, developed jointly with J.-L. Verdier, to the difference case. This approach allows us to characterize the corresponding spectral curves and find new classes of difference elliptic finite-gap operators which are difference analogs of the currently known elliptic finite-gap Schrödinger operators.

articleTitle: The zero-dispersion limit for the odd flows in the focusing Zakharov-Shabat hierarchy
abstract: We present a numerical and theoretical study of the zero-dispersion limit of the focusing Zakharov-Shabat hierarchy, which includes nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) and modified Korteweg-de Vries (mKdV) flows as its second and third members. All the odd flows in the hierachy are shown to preserve real-valued data. We establish the zero-dispersion limit of all the nontrivial conserved densities and associated fluxes for these odd flows for a large class of real-valued initial data which includes all “single hump” initial data. In particular, it is done for the “focusing” mKdV flow. The method is based on the Lax-Levermore KdV strategy, but here it is carried out in the context of a nonselfadjoint spectral problem. We find that after an algebraic transformation, the limiting dynamics of the mKdV equation is identical to that of the KdV equation.

articleTitle: Rational solutions of the Garnier system in terms of Schur polynomials
abstract: We present a family of rational solutions of the Garnier system H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> and show that the corresponding τ-functions form special polynomials R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m,n</inf>(m,n ∈ ℤ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">≥0</inf>) under a certain normalization. We give an explicit formula for the special polynomials R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m,n</inf> in terms of the Schur polynomial attached to a rectangular Young diagram.

articleTitle: A combinatorial approach to orthogonal exponentials
abstract: We prove that a symmetric strictly convex set with a smooth boundary in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup> can possess no more than finitely many orthogonal exponentials, unless d = 1 mod(4). In such case, the nonexistence theorem is true for a large class of bodies, including the d-dimensional ball. Otherwise, any infinite set of the corresponding exponents necessarily turns out to be a subset of some one-dimensional lattice. We provide examples of convex bodies of revolution in the above dimensions, for which infinite sets of orthogonal exponentials exist. The analysis is reduced to one dimension by studying the distance set of the putative set of exponents with respect to an appropriate metric. A combinatorial principle due to Erdös lies at the heart of the investigation. According to this principle, if the distance set of an infinite set in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup> is a subset of the integers, then the set itself is a subset of some one-dimensional lattice.

articleTitle: Geometry of Hilbert modular varieties over totally ramified primes
abstract: We study mod p Hilbert modular varieties associated to a totally real field L of degree g under the assumption that p is maximally ramified in O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>, the ring of algebraic integers of L. We associate to each O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>-abelian variety A over an F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>-algebra integer invariants 0 ≤ j ≤ n ≤ g−j that are used to define disjoint locally closed sets W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(j,n)</inf> of the moduli space. The invariants encode some of the structure of H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>(A, O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf>) as an O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>[F]-module. We prove that the sets W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(j,n)</inf> are nonempty, regular subvarieties of dimension g−(j+n). Moreover, the Newton polygon is constant on W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(j,n)</inf> having two slopes (λ(n), 1−λ(n)), each with multiplicity g, where λ(n) = min(1/2, n/g). Using Hecke correspondences at p and Moret-Bailly families, we prove that the collection {W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(j,n)</inf>: 0 ≤ j ≤ n ≤ g−j} is indeed a stratification: the boundary is a union of strata. Furthermore, the singularity stratification of Deligne-Pappas, the Newton stratification, and the a-number stratification, all have a simple expression as a union of our strata. We affirm general conjectures on Newton strata for this class of varieties, that they form a stratification, that they have the expected dimension (each strata being of codimension 1 in the previous strata), and that the Grothendieck conjecture holds.

articleTitle: Abelianizing the real permutation action via blowups
abstract: We present an abelianization of the permutation action of the symmetric group S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> on ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> in analogy to the Batyrev abelianization construction for finite group actions on complex manifolds. The abelianization is provided by a particular De Concini-Procesi wonderful model for the braid arrangement. In fact, we show a stronger result, namely that stabilizers of points in the arrangement model are isomorphic to direct products of ℤ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. To prove that, we develop a combinatorial framework for explicitly describing the stabilizers in terms of automorphism groups of set diagrams over families of cubes.We observe that the natural nested set stratification on the arrangement model is not stabilizer distinguishing with respect to the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>-action, that is, stabilizers of points are not in general isomorphic on open strata. Motivated by this structural deficiency, we furnish a new stratification of the De Concini-Procesi arrangement model that distinguishes stabilizers.

articleTitle: Discrete and smooth orthogonal systems: C∞-approximation
abstract: Discrete conjugate systems are quadrilateral nets with all planar faces. Discrete orthogonal systems are defined by the additional property of all faces being concircular. Their geometric properties allow one to consider them as proper discretization of conjugate, respectively, orthogonal coordinate systems of classical differential geometry. We develop techniques that allow us to extend this known qualitative analogy to rigorous convergence results. In particular, we prove the C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup>-convergence of discrete conjugate/orthogonal coordinate systems to smooth ones. We also show how to construct the approximating discrete nets. Coordinate systems and their transformations are treated on an equal footing, and the approximation results hold for transformations as well.

articleTitle: Real and global lifts from PGL3 to G2
abstract: First, we study the correspondence for real groups and show that it is functorial for spherical representations. Then, for cuspidal forms, we show that the lift is nonzero and cuspidal.

articleTitle: Symmetric polynomials vanishing on thediagonals shifted by roots of unity
abstract: For a pair of positive integers (k,r) with r ≥ 2 such that k+1 and r−1 are relatively prime, we describe the space of symmetric polynomials in variables x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> which vanish at all diagonals of codimension k of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_i=tq^{s_i}\text{?}x_{i-1}$</tex> , i=2,…,k+1, where t and q are primitive roots of unity of orders k+1 and r−1.

articleTitle: Noncommutative compactifications and elliptic curves
abstract: We introduce noncommutative degenerations of elliptic curves over local fields. Corresponding objects are close relatives of noncommutative tori of Connes and Rieffel.

articleTitle: The uncertainty principle for certain densities
abstract: We prove a new version of the uncertainty principle of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\int{\vert f\vert}^2\lesssim\int_{E^c}{\vert f\vert}^2+\int_{\Sigma^c}{\vert\widehat f\vert}^2$</tex> , where the sets E and Σ are ε-thin in the following sense: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\vert E\cap D{(x,\rho_1{(x)})}\vert}\text{?}\leq\text{?}\varepsilon{\vert D{(x,\rho_1{(x)})}\vert}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\vert\Sigma\cap D{(x,\rho_2{(x)})}\vert}\text{?}\leq\varepsilon{\vert D{(x,\rho_2{(x)})}\vert}$</tex> . This is an intermediate result between Logvinenko-Sereda's and Wolff's versions of the uncertainty principle.

articleTitle: Geometry of meromorphic functions and intersections onmoduli spaces of curves
abstract: We study relations between intersection numbers on moduli spaces of curves and Hurwitz numbers. First, we prove two formulas expressing Hurwitz numbers of (generalized) polynomials via intersections on moduli spaces of curves. Then we show how intersection numbers can be expressed via Hurwitz numbers. And then we obtain an algorithm expressing intersection numbers <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\langle\tau_{n,m}\prod\nolimits_{i=1}^{r-1}\tau_{0,i}^{k_i}\rangle_g$</tex> via correlation functions of primaries.

articleTitle: On a question of Dusa McDuff
abstract: Consider the 2n-dimensional closed ball B of radius 1 in the 2n-dimensional symplectic cylinder Z = D×ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n−2</sup> over the closed disc D of radius 1. We construct for each ε > 0 a Hamiltonian deformation φ of B in Z of energy less than ε such that the area of each intersection of φ(B) with the disc D × {x},x ∈ ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n−2</sup>, is less than ε. The construction involves the development of new symplectic embedding techniques.

articleTitle: A multiplier estimate of the Schwarzian derivative of univalent functions
abstract: The Schwarzian derivative of functions univalent in the unit disk is estimated as a multiplier between certain weighted Bergman spaces. As an application of these estimates, we find new bounds for the integral means spectrum of derivatives of univalent functions.

articleTitle: Abelian ideals of a Borel subalgebra and long positive roots
abstract: Let b be a Borel subalgebra of a simple Lie algebra g and let Ab denote the set of all Abelian ideals of b. We consider Ab as poset with respect to inclusion, the zero ideal being the unique minimal element of Ab. We show that there is a natural mapping τ from the set of all nontrivial Abelian ideals to the set of long positive roots. Each fibre of τ is a poset in its own right, and it is proved that this fibre has a unique maximal and a unique minimal element. If I is a maximal Abelian ideal, then we show that τ(I) is a (long) simple root. As a consequence, we deduce that restricting τ to the set of maximal Abelian ideals yields a one-to-one correspondence between the maximal Abelian ideals and the long simple roots. An explicit description of the minimal and the maximal ideal corresponding to a long root is given.

articleTitle: A supersingular K3 surface in characteristic 2 and the Leech lattice
abstract: We construct a K3 surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2, which contains two sets of 21 disjoint smooth rational curves such that each curve from one set intersects exactly 5 curves from the other set. This configuration is isomorphic to the configuration of points and lines on the projective plane over the finite field of 4 elements. The surface admits a finite automorphism group isomorphic to PGL(3,F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)· 2 such that a subgroup PGL(3,F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) acts on the configuration of each set of 21 smooth rational curves, and the additional element of order 2 interchanges the two sets. The Picard lattice of the surface is a reflective sublattice of an even unimodular lattice II<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,25</inf> of signature (1,25) and the classes of the 42 curves correspond to some Leech roots in II<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,25</inf>.

articleTitle: t-analogues des opérateurs d'écrantage associés aux q-caractères
abstract: Nous proposons des opérateurs d'écrantage pour la théorie des q,t-caractères de Nakajima (2001), analogues aux opérateurs d'écrantage de Frenkel et Reshetikhin relatifs à leur théorie des q-caractères pour les représentations de dimension finie des algèbres affines quantifiées (Frenkel et Reshetikhin 1999), avec en particulier les mêmes propriétés de symétrie. La théorie de Nakajima, établie dans le cas simplement laçé, utilise des anneaux non-commutatifs. Nous aurons ainsi à considérer des bimodules adaptés à ces structures, mais notre construction étant purement algébrique, elle est étendue au cas non-simplement laçé.Frenkel and Reshetikhin introduced screening operators related to q-characters of finite dimensional representations of quantum affine algebras (Frenkel and Reshetikhin 1999). We propose t-analogs of screening operators related to Nakajima's q,t-characters (2001) with the same properties of symmetry. Nakajima's approach is geometric and deals with the simply laced case. He used non-commutative rings, so we propose bimodules. But our construction is purely algebraic, and can be extended to the non-simply laced case.

articleTitle: Integrals of automorphic Green's functions associatedto Heegner divisors
abstract: We find explicit formulas for the degrees of Heegner divisors on arithmetic quotients of the orthogonal group O(2,p) and for the integrals of certain automorphic Green's functions associated to Heegner divisors. The latter quantities are important in the study of the arithmetic degrees of Heegner divisors in the context of Arakelov geometry. In particular, we obtain a different proof and a generalization of results of Kudla relating these quantities to the Fourier coefficients of certain nonholomorphic Eisenstein series of weight 1+p/2 for the metaplectic group Mp<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(ℤ).

articleTitle: Navigating the Cayley graph of SL2(Fp)
abstract: We present a probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm to find a path of length O(logp log logp) between any two vertices of the Cayley graph of SL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>) with respect to the generators <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\begin{array}{cc}1&1\\0&1\end{array})$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\begin{array}{cc}1&0\\1&1\end{array})$</tex> .

articleTitle: Structure constants for Hecke and representation rings
abstract: In 2002, Kapovich, Leeb, and Millson studied certain structure constants for two related rings: the spherical Hecke algebra of a split connected reductive group over a local non-Archimedean field, and the representation ring of the Langlands dual group. The structure constants of the former are defined relative to characteristic functions of double cosets, and the latter relative to highest weight representations. They proved that the nonvanishing of one of the latter structure constants always implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding former one. For GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, the reverse implication also holds, and is due to P. Hall. Both proofs are combinatorial in nature. In this paper, we provide geometric proofs for both results, using affine Grassmannians. We also provide some additional results concerning minuscule coweights and the equidimensionality of the fibers of certain Bott-Samelson resolutions of affine Schubert varieties for GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>.

articleTitle: On the topology of Lagrangian Milnor fibres
abstract: We study local deformations of singular Lagrangian complete intersections satisfying some nondegeneracy condition. We prove that for a Lagrangian deformation which is infinitesimally Lagrange-versal, the space of relative infinitesimal Lagrangian deformations is a free module over the base of the deformation. In case the deformation is a smoothing, this result implies that the first Betti number of a smoothing is equal to the dimension of the base of a Lagrangian miniversal deformation of the original Lagrangian variety.

articleTitle: Global stability of distributions of higher corank of derivedlength one
abstract: We consider tangent distributions of corank greater than one, each of whose first derived distributions, coincides with the tangent bundle of the underlying manifold. We study a global stability of such distributions. We prove that a one-parameter family of such distributions is described by using a global isotopy of the underlying manifold if the family has a constant integrable subdistribution of corank one. Furthermore, by giving an essential meaning of the subdistribution above from another perspective, we obtain a relation between the result mentioned above and the Gray theorem.

articleTitle: Inequality for Voiculescu's free entropy in terms of Brown measure
abstract: We study Voiculescu's microstate free entropy for a single nonselfadjoint random variable. The main result is that certain additional constraints on eigenvalues of microstates do not change the free entropy. Our tool is the method of random regularization of Brown measure, which was introduced recently by Haagerup and further developed by the author. As a simple application, we present an upper bound for the free entropy of a single nonselfadjoint operator in terms of its Brown measure and the second moment. Furthermore, we show that this inequality becomes an equality for a class of DT-operators, which was introduced recently by Dykema and Haagerup (2001).

articleTitle: Dimension of pluriharmonic measure and polynomial endomorphisms of ℂn
abstract: Let F be a polynomial endomorphism of ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> which extends holomorphically to ℂℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>. We prove that the dimension of μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>, the pluriharmonic measure on the boundary of the filled Julia set of F, is bounded above by 2n − 1.

articleTitle: Asymptotic analysis of (partially) orthogonal polynomials associated with root systems
abstract: A system of partially ordered polynomials will be referred to as partially orthogonal if the polynomials are orthogonal when comparable in the partial order. We present a formula describing the asymptotics for large degrees of a class of (partially) orthogonal multivariate polynomials associated with root systems. As an application, the asymptotics of the Macdonald polynomials is determined.

articleTitle: On the classification of multiplicity-free exterior algebras
abstract: We uniformly describe the irreducible character decompositions of the exterior algebras of two families of representations of semisimple Lie algebras. This simplifies parts of Howe's classification of skew multiplicity-free actions.

articleTitle: Module categories over the Drinfeld double of a finite group
abstract: We classify the module categories over the Drinfeld double (possibly twisted) of a finite group. We study in detail the case of the symmetric group in three letters.

articleTitle: Models for real subspace arrangements and stratified manifolds
abstract: We consider a central subspace and half-space arrangement A in Euclidean vector space V, and let M(A) be its complement. We construct some compactifications for the C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup>-manifold M(A)/ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>. They turn out to be C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup>-manifolds with corners whose boundary is determined by simple combinatorial data. This generalizes a construction described by Kontsevich in his paper on deformation quantization of Poisson manifolds. Then, we extend the construction to more general objects, that is, stratified real manifolds whose stratification locally looks like the one induced by an arrangement of linear (half-) spaces. The models we obtain are again C∞-manifolds with corners equipped with a nice combinatorial description of the boundary.

articleTitle: Almost modular functions and the distribution of n2x modulo one
abstract: For every irrational x, the sequence n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>x(n=1,2,3,…) is equidistributed modulo one: the number of n=1,…,N for which the fractional part of n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>x is contained in a subinterval [a,b] of the unit interval [0,1] is approximately N(b−a) for N large. We are here interested in the error term of this distribution, that is, the difference between the actual number and N(b−a). Our central result is that the error term can be identified with an almost modular function and therefore has a limit distribution as N→∞ for x random in [0,1].

articleTitle: Periods and Igusa local zeta functions
abstract: We show that the coefficients in the Laurent series of the Igusa local zeta functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I{(s)}=\int_cf^s\omega$</tex> are periods. This is proved by first showing the existence of functional equations for these functions. This will be used to show in a subsequent paper (by P. Brosnan) that certain numbers occurring in Feynman amplitudes (up to Gamma factors) are periods. We also give several examples of our main result, and one example showing that Euler's constant γ is an exponential period.

articleTitle: A parametrization of the theta divisor of the quartic double solid
abstract: Let M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf>(2;0, 3) be the moduli space of rank-2 stable vector bundles with Chern classes c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>=0, c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>=3 on the Fano threefold X, the double solid ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> of index two. We prove that the vector bundles obtained by Serre's construction from smooth elliptic quintic curves on X form an open part of an irreducible component M of M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf>(2;0, 3) and that the Abel-Jacobi map φ: M → J(X) into the intermediate Jacobian J(X) of X defined by the second Chern class is generically finite of degree 84 onto a translate Θ + const of the theta divisor. We also prove that the family of elliptic quintics on a general X is irreducible and of dimension 10.

articleTitle: Fatou's theorems and Hardy-type spaces foreigenfunctions of the invariant differential operators on symmetric spaces
abstract: We prove a Fatou-type theorem on a Riemannian symmetric space of the noncompact type and characterize the image of the Poisson transform of L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>-functions on the maximal boundary as a Hardy-type space.

articleTitle: Quasi-invariants and quantum integrals of the deformed Calogero-Moser systems
abstract: The rings of quantum integrals of the generalized Calogero-Moser systems related to the deformed root systems A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(m) and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(m,l) with integer multiplicities and corresponding algebras of quasi-invariants are investigated. In particular, it is shown that these algebras are finitely generated and free as the modules over certain polynomial subalgebras (Cohen-Macaulay property). The proof follows the scheme proposed by Etingof and Ginzburg in the Coxeter case. For two-dimensional systems the corresponding Poincaré series and the deformed m-harmonic polynomials are explicitly computed.

articleTitle: Semiclassical propagation on $\vert\text{log?}\hslash\vert$ time scales
abstract: We study the quantum evolution of a coherent state originally located in phase space on the unstable fixed point of a multiple well potential in one dimension. We show that, for sufficiently long times, the coherent state splits into two distinct components, each of which localizes semiclassically on a neighbouring unstable fixed point. Moreover, we show that during the transition the coherent state is distributed along the classical trajectory joining the two unstable points according to a density which we compute explicitly. At the times during which we explore the quantum dynamics of the coherent state, it is no longer determined by the classical dynamics of its center, but rather by the classical dynamics of the trajectories that are at a distance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt\hslash$</tex> of its center.

articleTitle: Hölder continuity of the integrated density of states for some random operators at all energies
abstract: We prove that the integrated density of states of random Schrödinger operators with Anderson-type potentials on L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup>), for d ≥ 1, is locally Hölder continuous at all energies for d ≥ 2, and Lipschitz continuous at all energies for d = 1. The single-site potential u must be nonnegative and compactly supported, and the distribution of the random variable must be absolutely continuous with a bounded, compactly supported density. We also prove continuity of the integrated density of states at all energies for random Anderson-type perturbations of the Landau Hamiltonian in two dimensions, and Hölder continuity under an additional rational flux condition.

articleTitle: Asymptotics of the partition function for random matrices via Riemann-Hilbert techniques and applications to graphical enumeration
abstract: We study the partition function from random matrix theory using a well-known connection to orthogonal polynomials, and a recently developed Riemann-Hilbert approach to the computation of detailed asymptotics for these orthogonal polynomials. We obtain the first proof of a complete large N expansion for the partition function, for a general class of probability measures on matrices, originally conjectured by Bessis, Itzykson, and Zuber (1980). We prove that the coefficients in the asymptotic expansion are analytic functions of parameters in the original probability measure, and that they are generating functions for the enumeration of labelled maps according to genus and valence. Central to the analysis is a large N expansion for the mean density of eigenvalues, uniformly valid on the entire real axis.

articleTitle: Cells in quantum affine sln
abstract: We study Lusztig's theory of cells for quantum affine sl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>. Using the geometric construction of the quantum group due to Lusztig, and independently Ginzburg and Vasserot, we describe explicitly the two-sided cells, the number of left cells in a two-sided cell, and the asymptotic algebra, verifying the conjectures of Lusztig.

articleTitle: Exceptional characters and prime numbers in arithmetic progressions
abstract: We consider some very strong statements about the distribution of primes which can be deduced from the assumption of the existence of exceptional zeros of Dirichlet L-functions. In this paper we consider the distribution of primes in arithmetic progressions and show that, under such an assumption, one can deduce the expected asymptotics in certain cases where the modulus of the progression is so large that even the GRH tells us nothing.

articleTitle: Classical and quantum scattering for a class of long range random potentials
abstract: We prove an almost sure existence of the modified wave operators for a class of Schrödinger operators with random long range potentials. The assumed decay of potential at infinity places it beyond the threshold of the standard class of long range potentials as described in the work of Buslaev-Matveev, Alsholm-Kato, and Hörmander. We develop an approach to quantum scattering which relies on averaging of potential over classical random trajectories. We also establish classical scattering for corresponding classical hamiltonians.

articleTitle: Towards an intersection homology theory for real algebraicvarieties
abstract: We consider equivariant intersection homology of stratified spaces with an involution. Specialization gives a good intersection homology theory with 2-torsion coefficients of the set of fixed points, but no grading. To get a degree filtration, we consider the equivariant cohomology sheaves on the quotient space with respect to the corresponding perverse t-structure. For algebraic varieties over the real numbers that admit a small resolution, it is shown that this procedure indeed provides the desired middle intersection homology theory, which even comes with a natural grading. In particular, it follows that the 2-torsion homology of a small resolution of a real algebraic variety is independent of the small resolution.

articleTitle: Frobenius distributions of elliptic curves over finite prime fields
abstract: We study the number H(t,p) of isomorphism classes of elliptic curves with Frobenius trace t ∈ ℤ over the finite field F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>. It may be predicted through a probabilistic model based on the frequencies of matrices in GL(2,ℤ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ℓ</inf>) with characteristic polynomial X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-tX+p, for primes ℓ ≠ p. We describe the asymptotics of the summatory function H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>(x) = ∑ H(t,p) (where p runs through the primes less than x ∈ ℝ). It turns out that the likelihood of a given t ∈ ℤ as a Frobenius trace is proportional to w(t)=∏ ((ℓ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>−ℓ)/(ℓ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>−ℓ−1))(ℓ|t,ℓ prime).

articleTitle: Field algebras
abstract: A field algebra is a noncommutative generalization of a vertex algebra. In this paper, we develop foundations of the theory of field algebras.

articleTitle: Morse functions on Su(n)2g and reduction
abstract: We study some Morse-Bott functions on Su(n). By composing it with the moment map of the quasi-Hamiltonian spaces Su(n)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2g</sup>, we obtain generalised Morse-Bott functions on Su(2)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2g</sup> and Su(3)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2g</sup>. As an application we get a geometric interpretation of the injectivity of the restriction map in the reduction of these spaces at the identity matrix.

articleTitle: The Wilson function transform
abstract: Two unitary integral transforms with a very well poised <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>-function as a kernel are given. For both integral transforms the inverse is the same as the original transform after an involution on the parameters. The <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>-function involved can be considered as a nonpolynomial extension of the Wilson polynomial, and is therefore called a Wilson function. The two integral transforms are called a Wilson function transform of types I and II. Furthermore, a few explicit transformations of hypergeometric functions are calculated, and it is shown that the Wilson function transform of type I maps a basis of orthogonal polynomials onto a similar basis of polynomials.

articleTitle: Wilson's Grassmannian and a noncommutative quadric
abstract: Let the group μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> of m th roots of unity act on the complex line by multiplication. This gives a μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>-action on Diff, the algebra of polynomial differential operators on the line. Following Crawley-Boevey and Holland (1998), we introduce a multiparameter deformation D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">τ</inf> of the smash product Diff #μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>. Our main result provides natural bijections between (roughly speaking) the following spaces: (1) μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>-equivariant version of Wilson's adelic Grassmannian of rank r ; (2) rank r projective D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">τ</inf>-modules (with generic trivialization data); (3) rank r torsion-free sheaves on a “noncommutative quadric” ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> × <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">τ</inf>ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>; (4) disjoint union of Nakajima quiver varieties for the cyclic quiver with m vertices. The bijection between (1) and (2) is provided by a version of Riemann-Hilbert correspondence between D-modules and sheaves. The bijections between (2), (3), and (4) were motivated by our previous work Quiver varieties and a noncommutative ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (2002). The resulting bijection between (1) and (4) reduces, in the very special case: r=1 and μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>={1}, to the partition of (rank 1) adelic Grassmannian into a union of Calogero-Moser spaces discovered by Wilson. This gives, in particular, a natural and purely algebraic approach to Wilson's result (1998).

articleTitle: Symmetries and solutions of Getzler's equation forCoxeter and extended affine Weyl Frobenius manifolds
abstract: The G-function associated with the semisimple Frobenius manifold C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>/W (where W is a Coxeter group or an extended affine Weyl group) is studied. The general form of the G-function is given in terms of a logarithmic singularity over caustics in the manifold. The main result in this paper is a universal formula for the G-function corresponding to the Frobenius manifold <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{C}^{n}/\widetilde{W}^{(k)}(A_{n-1})$</tex> , where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\widetilde W}^{(k)}{(A_{\text{?}n-1})}$</tex> is a certain extended affine Weyl group (or, equivalently, corresponding to the Hurwitz space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\widehat M}_{0;k-1,n-k-1}$</tex> ), together with the general form of the G-function in terms of data on caustics. Symmetries of the G-function are also studied.

articleTitle: Central embedding problems, the arithmetic lifting property, and tame extensions of ℚ
abstract: For every n ≠ 4,6,7, we prove that the arithmetic lifting property holds for all finite central extensions of the alternating group A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> over every field of characteristic 0. We also prove that tameness can be preserved when solving properly finite central embedding problems over ℚ. As a consequence of a regular version of this, we obtain the existence of infinitely many linearly disjoint tame Galois realizations of G over ℚ, for every finite central extension group G of each of the following groups: the alternating and symmetric groups A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> for every n, and the Mathieu groups M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>.

articleTitle: Lie algebras associated to fiber-type arrangements
abstract: Given a hyperplane arrangement in a complex vector space of dimension ℓ, there is a natural associated “redundant” arrangement of codimension k subspaces in a complex vector space of dimension kℓ. Topological invariants of the complement of this subspace arrangement are related to those of the complement of the original hyperplane arrangement. In particular, if the hyperplane arrangement is fiber-type, then, apart from grading, the Lie algebra obtained from the descending central series for the fundamental group of the complement of the hyperplane arrangement is isomorphic to the Lie algebra of primitive elements in the homology of the loop space for the complement of the associated subspace arrangement. Furthermore, this last Lie algebra is given by the homotopy groups modulo torsion of the loop space of the complement of the subspace arrangement. Looping further yields an associated Poisson algebra which satisfies generalizations of the “universal infinitesimal Poisson braid relations.”

articleTitle: Lefschetz properties for arithmetic real and complex hyperbolic manifolds
abstract: We state new conjectures, of “Lefschetz type,” on the relationships between the (co)homology of arithmetic real and complex hyperbolic manifolds and the (co)homology of their totally geodesic subspaces. We prove particular cases of these conjectures by relating them to conjectures jointly made with Clozel on the automorphic spectrum of arithmetic real and complex hyperbolic manifolds, which appear to be particular cases of Arthur's conjectures of which some new approximations were obtained by Bergeron and Clozel.

articleTitle: Criteria to the Poincaré inequality associated with Dirichlet forms in ℝd, d ≥ 2
abstract: We study the compactness of the resolvent of Witten Laplacians on 0-forms and more generally the validity of the Poincaré inequality for Dirichlet forms in finite dimension. We are interested in the case where some known sufficient condition becomes degenerate. For some classes of polyhomogeneous functions, we get simple conditions which are necessary and sufficient for the Poincaré inequality.

articleTitle: Existence of solutions for a class of hyperbolic systems of conservation laws in several space dimensions
abstract: In a recent paper, Bressan has shown that the Cauchy problem for the system of conservation laws <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\partial_t\text{?}u_i+\sum\nolimits_{\alpha=1}^n\partial_{x_\alpha}{(f_\alpha{({\vert u\vert})}u_i)}=0$</tex> , <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_i{\text{?}(0,\cdot)}={\overline u}_i\text{?}{(\cdot)}$</tex> can be ill posed for suitable Lipschitz flux functions f and initial data <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline u\in L^\infty$</tex> which are bounded away from 0. In the final part of his paper, Bressan points out that the Cauchy problem could be well posed for BV initial data. In this paper, we prove a general existence result for bounded weak solutions of the Cauchy problem for the system of conservation laws assuming that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\in W_{\text loc}^{1,\infty}$</tex> and that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline u\in L^\infty$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\vert\overline u\vert}\geq c>0\text{?}\mathscr{L}^n$</tex> —a.e. and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\vert\overline u\vert}\in{\text{BV}}_\text loc$</tex> . Our proof relies on recent results of the first author, which extend the DiPerna-Lions theory of ODE with discontinuous coefficients to BV vector fields satisfying natural L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup> bounds on the distributional divergence.

articleTitle: The Golinskii-Ibragimov method and a theorem of Damanik and Killip
abstract: In 1971, Golinskii and Ibragimov proved that if the Verblunsky coefficients, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\{\alpha_n\}}_{n=0}^\infty$</tex> , of a measure dμ on ∂D obey <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum\nolimits_{n=0}^\infty n{\vert\alpha_n\vert}^2<\infty$</tex> , then the singular part, dμ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>, of dμ vanishes. We show how to use extensions of their ideas to discuss various cases where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum\nolimits_{n=0}^Nn{\vert\alpha_n\vert}^2$</tex> diverges logarithmically. As an application, we provide an alternative to a part of the proof of a recent theorem of Damanik and Killip.

articleTitle: Hodge-theoretic invariants for algebraic cycles
abstract: We use Hodge theory to define a filtration on the Chow groups of a smooth, projective algebraic variety. Assuming the generalized Hodge conjecture and a conjecture of Bloch-Beilinson, we show that this filtration terminates at the codimension of the algebraic cycle class, thus providing a complete set of period-type invariants for a rational equivalence class of algebraic cycles.

articleTitle: Topological robotics: motion planning in projective spaces
abstract: We study an elementary problem of the topological robotics: rotation of a line, which is fixed by a revolving joint at a base point. One wants to bring the line from its initial position A to a final position B by a continuous motion in space. The ultimate goal is to construct a motion planning algorithm which will perform this task once the initial position A and the final position B are presented. Any such motion planning algorithm must have instabilities, that is, the motion of the system will be discontinuous as a function of A and B. A general approach to study instabilities of robot motion was suggested in the work of M. Farber. With any path-connected topological space X, one associates a number TC(X), called the topological complexity ofX. This number is of fundamental importance for the motion planning problem: TC(X) determines character of instabilities which have all motion planning algorithms in X. The motion planning problem of moving a line in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n+1</sup>, which we study in this paper, reduces to a topological problem of calculating the topological complexity of the real projective space TC(ℝℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>. We compute the number TC(ℝℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> for all n ≤ 23. Surprisingly, the problem of finding a general formula for TC(ℝℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> turns out to be quit difficult. One of the main results of this paper claims that for n ≠ 1, 3, 7, the number TC(ℝℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> coincides with the smallest integer k such that the projective space ℝℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> admits an immersion into ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k−1</sup>. This means that our problem of finding TC(ℝℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> is equivalent to the immersion problem for real projective spaces. For the remarkable special values n=1,3,7, the answer is very simple: TC(ℝℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>) = n=1. We show that for n ≤ 8 explicit motion planning algorithms for moving lines in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> can be built by using multiplication of the complex numbers, the quaternions, and the Cayley numbers.

articleTitle: Local estimates for a class of fully nonlinear equations arising from conformal geometry
abstract: We establish local gradient estimates for fully nonlinear partial differential equations involving elementary symmetric functions of Schouten tensor in conformal geometry. We also obtain local second derivative estimates for solutions of these equations.

articleTitle: The number of linear series on curves with given ramification
abstract: We use Eisenbud and Harris' theory of limit linear series (1986) to show that for a general smooth curve of genus g in characteristic 0, with general points P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> and indices e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum\nolimits_i{(e_i-1)}=2d-2-g$</tex> , <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_d^1\text{?}{(C,{\{{(P_i,e_i)}\}}_i)}$</tex> is made up of reduced points. We give a formula for the number of points, showing that it agrees with various known special cases. We also conjecture a corresponding reducedness result and formula for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g_d^r$</tex> 's of any dimension, and reduce this to the case of three points on ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, where one needs no longer consider moduli or generality.

articleTitle: On the symmetric powers of cusp forms on GL(2) of icosahedral type
abstract: We study the symmetric powers of strongly modular icosahedral representations ρ of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Gal}{(\overline F/F)}$</tex> , where F is a number field, and their twisted L-functions. We prove that for such ρ, there exists a cuspidal automorphic representation Π=Π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> ⊗ Π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf> of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>(A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf>) such that L(s, sym<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> ρ))=L(s, Π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>). One knows that sym<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> ρ is twist equivalent to ρ′ ⊗ sym<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ρ for another modular icosahedral representation ρ′, and our theorem is a special case of a cuspidality criterion formulated and proved in this paper, which may be of independent interest, for the Kim-Shahidi automorphic tensor product π ⊠ sym<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (π′), where π π′ are cuspidal automorphic representations of GL(2)/F. We also give a complete structure theory of modular icosahedral representations. As a result, we prove that L(s, sym<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>(ρ)⊗χ does not admit any Landau-Siegel zero when it is not divisible by L-functions of quadratic characters. In general, there is no such divisibility and there are no Landau-Siegel zeros for such L-functions.

articleTitle: Classification of simple modules over degenerate double affine Hecke algebras of type A
abstract: We study a class of representations over the degenerate (and nondegenerate) double affine Hecke algebra of gl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> by an algebraic method. As fundamental objects in this class, we introduce certain induced modules and study some of their properties. In particular, it is shown that these induced modules have unique simple quotient modules under certain conditions. Moreover, we show that any simple module in this class is obtained as such a simple quotient, and give a classification of all the simple modules.

articleTitle: Equivariant mirrors and the Virasoro conjecture for flag manifolds
abstract: We find an explicit description of all GL(n, ℝ)-Whittaker functions as oscillatory integrals and thus construct equivariant mirrors of flag manifolds. As a consequence, we prove the Virasoro conjecture for flag manifolds.

articleTitle: On the local well-posedness of the Benjamin-Ono equation in Hs(ℝ)
abstract: We prove that the Benjamin-Ono equation is locally well-posed for data in H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>(ℝ), s > 5/4. The proof depends crucially on the use of half Strichartz estimates for linear problems with variable coefficients.

articleTitle: Path model for a level-zero extremal weight module over a quantum affine algebra
abstract: We give a path model for a level-zero extremal weight module over a quantum affine algebra. By using this result, we prove branching rules for an extremal weight module and a fundamental representation of level zero with respect to the quantized universal enveloping algebra of a Levi subalgebra.

articleTitle: Koszul duality and equivariant cohomology for tori
abstract: Let T be a torus. We show that Koszul duality can be used to compute the equivariant cohomology of topological T-spaces as well as the cohomology of pullbacks of the universal T-bundle. The new features are that no further assumptions about the spaces are made and that the coefficient ring may be arbitrary. This gives in particular a Cartan-type model for the equivariant cohomology of a T-space with arbitrary coefficients. Our method works for intersection homology as well.

articleTitle: Nonrelativistic limit from Maxwell-Klein-Gordon and Maxwell-Dirac to Poisson-Schrödinger
abstract: We show that solutions for the system of Maxwell-Klein-Gordon and Maxwell-Dirac equations can be described by using a system of coupled Poisson and Schrödinger equations as the speed of light c tends to infinity, in the strong topology of the energy space, which is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot H^1\times H^{\text{?}1}$</tex> for the first system and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot H^1\times c^{\text{?}-1/2}H^{\text{?}1/2}+H^{\text{?}1}$</tex> for the second system. The two Schrödinger-Poisson systems recovered at the limit present some differences which can be interpreted physically.

articleTitle: Geometric crystal and tropical R for $D_n^{(1)}$
abstract: We construct a geometric crystal for the affine Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D_n^{(1)}$</tex> in the sense of Berenstein and Kazhdan. Based on a matrix realization including a spectral parameter, we prove uniqueness and explicit form of the tropical R, the birational map that intertwines products of the geometric crystals. The tropical R commutes with geometric Kashiwara operators and satisfies the Yang-Baxter equation. It is subtraction-free and yields a piecewise linear formula of the combinatorial R for crystals upon ultradiscretization.

articleTitle: Proper isometric actions of Thompson's groups on Hilbert space
abstract: The Thompson groups F, T, and V act properly and isometrically on Hilbert space. The associated 1-cocycle is described explicitly.

articleTitle: The Brauer group of analytic K3 surfaces
abstract: We show that for complex analytic K3 surfaces any torsion class in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^2{(X,\text{O}_X^\ast)}$</tex> comes from an Azumaya algebra. In other words, the Brauer group equals the cohomological Brauer group. For algebraic surfaces, such results go back to Grothendieck (1968). In our situation, we use twistor spaces to deform a given analytic K3 surface to suitable projective K3 surfaces, and then stable bundles and hyperholomorphy conditions to pass back and forth between the members of the twistor family.

articleTitle: Bases of representations of type A affine Lie algebras via quiver varieties and statistical mechanics
abstract: We relate two apparently different bases in the representations of affine Lie algebras of type A: one arising from statistical mechanics and the other from gauge theory. We show that the two are governed by the same combinatorics that also respects the weight space decomposition of the representations. In particular, we are able to give an alternative and much simpler geometric proof of the main result of E. Date et al. (1989) on the construction of bases of affine Lie algebra representations. At the same time, we give a simple parametrization of the irreducible components of Nakajima quiver varieties associated to infinite and cyclic quivers. We also define new varieties whose irreducible components are in one-to-one correspondence with the highest weight representations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\widehat{g\ell}}_{n+1}$</tex> .

articleTitle: Calabi quasimorphism and quantum homology
abstract: We prove that the group of area-preserving diffeomorphisms of the 2-sphere admits a nontrivial homogeneous quasimorphism to the real numbers with the following property: its value on any diffeomorphism supported in a sufficiently small open subset of the sphere equals to the Calabi invariant of the diffeomorphism. This result extends to more general symplectic manifolds: if a symplectic manifold is monotone and its quantum homology algebra is semisimple, we construct a similar quasimorphism on the universal cover of the group of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms.

articleTitle: Symmetric polynomials vanishing on the shifted diagonals and Macdonald polynomials
abstract: For each pair (k, r) of positive integers with r ≥ 2, we consider an ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_n^{(k,r)}$</tex> of the ring of symmetric polynomials. The ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_n^{(k,r)}$</tex> has a basis consisting of Macdonald polynomials P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</inf>(x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>;q,t) at t<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k+1</sup>q<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r−1</sup>=1, and is a deformed version of the one studied earlier by the authors (2002). In this paper, we give a characterization of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_n^{(k,r)}$</tex> in terms of explicit zero conditions on the k-codimensional shifted diagonals of the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_2=tq^{s_1}x_1,\dots,x_{k+1}=tq^{s_k}x_k$</tex> . The ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_n^{(k,r)}$</tex> may be viewed as a deformation of the space of correlation functions of an abelian current of the affine Lie algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\widehat{\text{s}\ell}}_r$</tex> . We give a brief discussion about this connection.
